issues.problem: The Extend slide offers only stretch tasks (A+B icons, design-your-own, shake) with no support tier for struggling learners, matching the R0 missing[] differentiation gap.
issues.fix: Add a paired support option (e.g. a pre-built remix project or a guided one-button build) so the core task stays reachable for all, as the upstream lessons embed support/stretch.

issues.problem: Evaluate relies on open reflective questions with no embedded success criterion or demo/exit-ticket/peer-share check, matching the R0 missing[] assessment gap.
issues.fix: Embed a brief observable demo check or oral exit ticket (e.g. 'press A and say what the micro:bit shows') in the Evaluate slot instead of only discussion prompts.

issues.problem: The input/output learning objectives state abstract definitions ('data sent to/from a computer') without a concrete hands-on anchor for ages 7-9.
issues.fix: Tie the definitions to a tangible physical example or unplugged action (e.g. pressing a real button, seeing a real light) before the abstract wording.

issues.problem: The 'examine the code' step reveals completed code with no prediction prompt, missing the cognitive-load-reducing 'predict before reveal' Think move.
issues.fix: Ask a short prediction ('what do you think the micro:bit shows when button A is pressed?') before opening the completed project.

issues.problem: No alternative input is offered for learners who struggle with button presses or fine motor control, leaving accessibility uncovered.
issues.fix: Suggest a touch-logo, sound, or external-switch alternative input for the shake/button extension to include fine-motor-challenged learners.

issues.problem: Share is a teacher-led Q&A revisiting objectives rather than a student peer-share or physical artefact show, omitting the relatedness/competence element and a peer-instruction misconception check.
issues.fix: Convert Share into a paired peer-share ('tell a partner one block you used and why') with a physical show of the badge.

issues.problem: The recap stresses the forever loop for animation while the new lesson teaches on-button event handlers, with no bridge explaining why reactive inputs use events rather than forever.
issues.fix: Add one sentence clarifying that button presses are events handled on demand, so they use on-button blocks instead of a forever loop.
